note: Window agent m0800-m0701, 2 Nov 2026: three corrections found with the replay of the draft and the pages opened in this run. [Seam agent sm-02, 3 Nov 2026: events/2 (Carchemish vassal of Assyria from 738) and events/3 (Sam'al from 740) reopen the tributary tints that m0900-m0801 events/0 and events/1 closed, and keyframe_overrides/1 and /2 keep the Neo-Assyrian -800 and -750 shapes off their land while they were independent (pages opened: Pisiri, Tiglath-Pileser III, Carchemish, Sam'al, Zincirli Expedition, USC Panamu II).]

region.text: the whole of the Magna Graecia region (Calabria, Apulia, Basilicata, Campania and all Sicily, 279 cells) that the -720 gain drew, less the Rhegium, Zancle and Naxos discs

events.note: -720: the dossier's gain 'the Achaean colonies of the Ionian coast of Italy' resolves the region 'Magna Graecia' (295 cells, the whole of southern Italy and Sicily) and so draws 279 cells to the aggregate for 11 years until the -709 keyframe drops them. The page has the Achaean wave 'concentrated initially on the Ionian coast' of Italy: Sybaris 'Others 721/720', Kroton 709/708, Taranto 706 (Jerome), Rhegium 'c. 730', all coastal foundations, 'Magna Graecia ... the coastal areas of Southern Italy'. Sybaris, Croton and Taras are dossiers of their own (found -720, -710, -706 with their discs), and Sicily other than the east-coast colonies is not Greek-held; this event takes the over-wide region back and keeps only the Rhegium, Zancle and Naxos discs.

region.text: the Matruh governorate (Qattara, Siwa and the Libyan plateau) outside Cliopatria's Kush shape of -700

events.note: -711: the Kush dossier's gain 'the Saite Delta' names the region 'Lower Egypt', which the gazetteer builds with the whole Matruh governorate, and its counterpart 'Twenty-fourth Dynasty of Egypt (Sais)' is a name, not a slug, so the gain took 509 unowned desert cells (about 129,000 km2) as a detached Kushite exclave 1,000 km from Nubia. The Delta itself is the 25th Dynasty's from -712 and Cliopatria's Kush shape of -700 holds only 15 Matruh cells. The page: Shebitku 'conquered the entire Nile Valley, including Upper and Lower Egypt, around 712 BC' and Shabaka 'brought the entire Nile Valley as far as the Delta under the empire of Kush'; it says nothing of the Western Desert, oases or Siwa.

region.text: Carchemish and its district on the west bank of the Euphrates (coordinates 36 49 46 N, 38 00 59 E on the page)

events.note: 738 BC: Pisiri of Carchemish is a tributary of Tiglath-Pileser III. Pisiri page: 'In 738 BC Pisiri was tributary to the Assyrian king Tiglath-Pileser III' (the king is named in Assyrian sources only for 738 and 717). The Tiglath-Pileser III page has Gurgum, Kummuh, Carchemish and Quwe paying tribute after the capture of Arpad in 740, without a year; the Carchemish page has Karkamish absent from Assyrian sources between Samsi-Adad V (824-811) and the mid-8th century. Opens the tributary tint that m0900-m0801 events/0 closed in -848; the dossier's own vassal_end of -717 closes it.

region.text: Sam'al round Zincirli Hoyuk in Gaziantep Province, 'near the Nur Mountains' in the Anti-Taurus (infobox coordinates 37 06 13 N, 36 40 43 E); a 40 km circle is the researcher's reading of a 'middle power' whose territories round Carchemish, Quwe and Adana the page does not delimit

events.note: 740 BC (campaign of 743-740): Tiglath-Pileser III installs Panamuwa II on the throne of Sam'al. Zincirli Expedition settlement-history page: Tiglath-pileser III 'installed Panamuwa II on the throne of Sam'al' during his campaign against a western coalition, dated 743-740 BCE; Panamuwa II 'was killed fighting alongside the Assyrians at Damascus' in 733/732 BCE; his son Barrakib 'was confirmed on the throne of Sam'al by Tiglath-pileser III' and called himself 'the servant of Tiglath-pileser'. The page gives no year inside 743-740, so the last one, the year of Arpad on the Tiglath-Pileser III page, is taken. The USC West Semitic Research Project page on Panamu II says the same ('loyalty as vassal to Tiglath Pileser III', killed in action on campaign in 732). Opens the tint that m0900-m0801 events/1 closed in -824; the dossier's own vassal_end of -717 closes it.

union.text: Lai, eastern Shandong on the tip of the peninsula bordering Qi
Tan, just east of Jinan, capital Mingshui (Zhangqiu)

correction.text: Qi as Cliopatria draws it in -750, without the land of Lai (to 567), Ji (to 690), Tan (to 684) and Sui (to 681), which Qi annexed in those years

keyframe_overrides.why: The Spring and Autumn table gives the annexations to Qi: Ji '690 BCE: to Qi', Tan '684 BCE: to Qi', Sui '681 BCE: to Qi', Lai '567 BCE: to Qi'. Cliopatria has no rows for these four states, so its Qi shape of -750 swallows their land, and the compiler's succession rule (R2) gave Qi 124 cells (Lai 98, Ji 14, Tan 9, Sui 3) at -750, so Lai, Ji, Tan and Sui vanished from the map 183 to 18 years before they ended. The Lai page: 'In 567 BC, Lai attacked Qi but was decisively defeated by Duke Ling of Qi', 'Qi more than doubled in size after annexing Lai'. Their own ledgers (loss to qi at 690, 684, 681, 567) hand the land to Qi at the right dates.

union.text: Carchemish and its district on the west bank of the Euphrates (the dossier's 60 km circle round 36 49 46 N, 38 00 59 E), north of the Til Barsip land that Assyria has held since the Bit Adini gain of 856
Sam'al round Zincirli Hoyuk in Gaziantep Province (the dossier's 40 km circle round 37 06 13 N, 36 40 43 E)

minus.text: Babylonia, a separate kingdom until 729, with Carchemish and Sam'al, which were independent kingdoms until Tiglath-Pileser III (-738 and -740)

correction.text: Assyria as the dossier draws it (without Babylonia until 729), and without Carchemish and Sam'al, which paid no tribute and kept their own kings until 740/738 and are then tributaries that keep their land (m0800-m0701 events/2 and events/3)

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's correction cuts only Babylonia from Cliopatria's shape (valid -800..-751). Since m0900-m0801 events/0 and events/1 closed the bridged Assyrian tints of Carchemish (848) and Sam'al (824), the shape's western part takes their land: both dossiers name the Neo-Assyrian Empire as successor, so the compiler's R2 hands Assyria their cells as direct land and both states vanish from the map until 717 (published packet: the -800 snap is 186 cells, against 151 in the window agent's report; carchemish / neo-assyrian-empire 22 and sam-al / neo-assyrian-empire 10 cell-years of R2). The pages have both independent: Carchemish page, Karkamish 'does not appear in Assyrian sources until the mid-8th century BC' bar 'a brief mention by Samsi-Adad V (824-811)', with the House of Astiruwa ruling from Astiruwa (ca 848-790) to Pisiri (Pisiri page); Sam'al page, 'Sam'al became independent after the death of Shalmaneser III' (824), and the Zincirli page has Tiglath-pileser III installing Panamuwa II in the campaign of 743-740. So their land is cut from the shape: Sam'al's whole 40 km circle (19 cells, all Sam'al's), Carchemish's 22 cells (the 60 km circle minus its southern strip, which is Bit Adini land Assyria took in 856 and keeps: 18 cells; a first cut of the whole circle had released them). From -740 (Sam'al) and -738 (Carchemish) they are vassals and keep their land by rule 4. The rest of the correction is unchanged.
